cohort: Women admitted in labor to hospitals (n = 2527) and birth centers (n = 8776)
finding: Women receiving care in birth centers had a 37-38% decreased odds of cesarean birth compared to those admitted to hospitals, suggesting that the entire birth center care model contributes to lower cesarean rates.
mod_finding: The study found that women receiving care in birth centers had a 37-38% decreased odds of cesarean delivery compared to those admitted to hospitals.
